questions.stem: During a fitness test, a student's breathing rate increases from 15 breaths/min at rest to 40 breaths/min during vigorous exercise. What is the primary reason for this increase?

options.text: To cool down the body by exhaling warm air
To increase oxygen intake and CO₂ removal to meet higher energy demands of muscles
To prevent lactic acid from entering the lungs
To increase the amount of glucose absorbed from the air

questions.explanation: During exercise, muscles need more energy, so the rate of respiration increases. This requires more oxygen and produces more CO₂. The increased breathing rate ensures more O₂ is delivered and more CO₂ is removed from the blood.

questions.stem: A PE teacher measures a student's heart rate before, during, and after exercise. The heart rate peaks during exercise and takes 5 minutes to return to resting rate afterwards. What does a faster recovery time indicate?

options.text: The student has a higher resting heart rate than average
The student is less physically fit
The student has a higher level of cardiovascular fitness
The student relied entirely on anaerobic respiration

questions.explanation: A faster recovery time (quicker return to resting heart rate) indicates better cardiovascular fitness. A fit person's heart is more efficient at pumping blood, so it can deliver oxygen and remove waste products more quickly, reducing recovery time.

questions.stem: An athlete notices that during a long-distance race, their muscles begin to ache even though they are still running at a steady pace. What is happening in their muscles?

options.text: Their muscles have run out of glucose completely
Aerobic respiration alone is insufficient, and anaerobic respiration is producing lactic acid
Their muscles have stopped respiring due to fatigue
Excess oxygen is damaging the muscle fibres

questions.explanation: Even at a steady pace, if oxygen demand exceeds supply, some anaerobic respiration occurs alongside aerobic respiration. The lactic acid produced builds up in the muscles, causing the aching sensation and eventually contributing to fatigue.

questions.stem: Blood is redirected away from the digestive system towards the muscles during exercise. Why is this beneficial for respiration in the muscles?

options.text: It prevents the digestion of proteins that muscles need
It delivers more oxygenated blood and glucose to the muscles for increased aerobic respiration
It reduces the production of carbon dioxide in the gut
It increases the temperature of the muscles to speed up diffusion

questions.explanation: During exercise, blood vessels supplying the muscles dilate (vasodilation) while those to less urgent organs constrict. This ensures muscles receive more oxygen and glucose — the reactants needed for aerobic respiration to meet increased energy demands.

questions.stem: Two students cycle at the same speed for 10 minutes. Student A has been training regularly for months; Student B rarely exercises. Which observation would you expect when comparing their results?

options.text: Student B would have a lower heart rate during exercise
Student A would produce more lactic acid during the exercise
Student A would have a lower heart rate during exercise and recover faster afterwards
Both students would show identical heart rate responses

questions.explanation: Regular training improves cardiovascular fitness — the heart becomes stronger and more efficient, delivering more oxygen per beat. Student A would therefore have a lower exercising heart rate (each beat delivers more blood) and recover more quickly afterwards.
